report.whatTheMapAsked:
It asked about **decay, in both directions at once**, and E6's signature mechanic is load-bearing in the strictest sense — it is the entire economy. A machine not struck for `windDownSeconds: 8` *exhausts*: harmless, undamageable, crawling at 0.2×, and **exempt from the 60-alive cap**, so the board piles up in plain sight. The idle probe is the proof and it is the loudest number on this contract: **35 kills and `gold: 0` across 98 seconds** with machines exhausting and nothing collecting them. `now.atomic.wrangle` publishes `captureRadius: 2.2` and the pen (`goldPerMachine: 1`, `tickSeconds: 15`), and `CAPTURE` — targetless, free, taken at **the hero** — is the only converter. Every penned machine pays for the rest of the run, so it is an opening move rather than a mid-game one: my pen reached **66 machines and granted 580 gold, out-earning the 730 I panned across five anchors**, with zero commute.

The objective is a different clock running the other way, and it is the most legible one I have ridden: `stablePrefix.mechanics.rules[2]` publishes `three_stake_hold` in full — `radius: 3`, `holdSeconds: 6`, `defenders: ["standing_structure", "active_hero"]`, `heroActiveDefenseSeconds: 5`, plus the claim, reset, pressure, loss and secure rules — so a rider working from the view alone has every number. `stake.timer` accrues toward 6 while a machine stands uncontested in the disc and **resets to 0** the instant any defender appears, and the loss needs **all three**. Because `contested()` tests only `active && hp > 0` within r3, a **10-gold palisade defends a stake exactly as well as a 125-gold turret** — the map's own briefing says so, and it is true in the code.

The era's lever is also a real trade rather than a free lunch, exactly as the source states it: `pressureTarget` routes one enemy in four (`PICNIC_STAKE_PRESS_WEIGHT 0.25`) at the nearest **undefended** stake, and `HeadlessContractSim:2042` **skips `handleEnemyContact` for any enemy that is pressing**. So defending stakes hands you back the fight you were being spared. I paid that deliberately: with the objective settled, every enemy pursued the hero, and 14 works held the line at 96 % health.

View fields that carried it: `now.atomic.picnicHold[]` (`claimed`, `contested`, `timer`, `position`), `now.atomic.wrangle.{captureRadius, pen}` and `now.atomic.exhausted`, `now.works.entries` (position + `wrecked` — the only way to see which stake is actually fenced), `now.seams[].active/x/z/anchorIndex` (an inactive seam publishes all three as `null`, and one non-finite number refuses the whole array silently), `now.gold` against `now.score.goldPanned`/`goldStolen`, `now.hero.hp/maxHp/x/z`, `now.orders[].status/reason`. Orders: **`CAPTURE`** (stacked 8 deep), `BUILD`, `HARVEST`, `MOVE_HERO`, `PICK_UPGRADE`, `BLAST_AT`, and one blank line at the boundary. There is no E6 verb beyond `CAPTURE`.

**My notebook remembers this map (generation 25, era 5) and it still plays the way I remember in its bones** — same three stakes, same six-second hold, same r3 rule, same wave-20 default, same pen economy, same two-id roster. The re-survey moved this map's rendering, not its rules. **This map was named as CURED this week, so: what its first minute actually did.** The hero walked into the west stake's disc by t = 2.83 and held it by the published `active_hero` rule (it auto-fires, and every hit refreshes the 5-second window). The Prospector walked 22.4 units to the only near live seam at (22, 8) and panned; **the east stake was claimed at or before t = 28.4 anyway**, because my fence money did not exist yet. Then the cure did exactly what pin #8 says it does: `pressureTarget` returns `null` for **every** enemy for `PICNIC_CLAIM_STANDDOWN_SECONDS = 20` after any claim, so the other two stakes were not handed over behind it — and my first two palisades were standing at t = 28.4, inside that window. **They then held for the remaining 571 seconds and were never touched again.** The stand-down is not a strategy, it is a reading window, and on this ride it is the difference between losing one stake and losing the map.
report.winnability: Secured, and the margin was **wide on survival, at the arithmetic ceiling on the score, and one stake thin on the objective**: every ranking axis is maxed (waves 20 and timeAlive 600.000 are pinned by the gate; 500 gold is `bankCap` 200 + 150 × 2 standing stockpiles, the most this contract can publish), the hero never dropped below 96.1 % and nothing was ever wrecked — but I finished holding **two of three stakes**, because my own suffix gate inverted the build order and the east fence arrived after the east stake had already fallen.
report.lessons:
- **A suffix gate on EQUAL-priced rungs builds the array backwards, and I re-introduced the bug my own generation 28 recorded.** Gating three 10-gold palisades at 30/20/10 in tour order (east, center, west) does not fire them together at 30 gold — the first *actionable* order owns the tick, so at 10 gold the rung gated at **10** fires, which is the one I listed **last**. My tour was east→center→west and my build order was west→center→east: the Prospector made the longest trip first and the nearest stake, 11.7 units from the seam, was fenced last and fell before its money existed. Generation 28 named the cure and I did not carry it: **plan-time affordability — emit `min(missing, floor(gold / cost))` rungs and gate only that batch** — or, on an equal-priced batch, gate them all at one unit and let array order decide.
- **On a map with an objective deadline inside the blind opening, optimise TIME-TO-FIRST, not the tour.** The first stake falls at ~t = 25 and view 2 does not arrive until t = 30, so the opening array is unattended across the whole decision. The tour-optimal gate saves ~15 seconds of walking and costs the first fence ~7 seconds of lateness; on this board the second number is the only one that can lose something.
- **Read the roster by INTERSECTION when the contract and `Balance` both declare one.** `WaveSystem.enemyRosterFor` filters the contract's `twist.enemyRoster` by the epoch mix's id list, so a variant present in `Balance.e6Roster.mixes.standard` but absent from the contract (here `glowjack`, the only `thief`) **can never spawn**. Two lists, one intersection — and that single read settled the wrecker question (palisades are permanent), the thief question (the stockpile is +90 net, not generation 106's 435-gold trap) and deleted `REPAIR_UNDER` from the design. Generation 82 learned not to read an early `threats.wreckers: 0` as a roster fact; the complement is **do not read either list alone, either.**
- **The map's own `mechanics.rules` published the whole objective, and the cheapest buildable that satisfies the predicate is the answer.** `defenders: ["standing_structure", "active_hero"]` with no hp, tier, kind or damage term means 10 gold defends a stake as well as 125. Find the predicate the objective actually evaluates and buy the cheapest thing that satisfies it.
- **The hero is a free stopgap wherever an objective's defender list includes it.** `contested()` reads "the hero landed a hit anywhere in the last 5 s AND the hero is inside this disc", and the headless hero auto-fires, so one `MOVE_HERO` at t = 0 held the west stake for nothing while the purse funded fences — then came home when `objectiveDone` flipped. Emitted **once**, dropped when parked, advanced only on a real `UNREACHABLE` record (never a ladder — generation 68 measured that as a shuttle that freezes the economy).
- **Check whether the objective's threat was also absorbing something.** `pressureTarget` returning `null` is what re-arms `handleEnemyContact`, so winning the objective *raises* the combat load by a quarter of the board. Price that before buying the fence, then buy the fence anyway when the loss condition is absolute and the combat is not.
- **A claimed stake is a retired rung, not a rung to retry.** `claimed` is one-way, so fencing it afterwards is pure waste; skipping it is what let the ladder move straight on to the stockpiles that are the actual score.
- **An era named for rebuilt maps can leave a map's rules untouched even when a pin NAMES the map — thirteenth heat running, and the first where the pin named my contract and the floor still settled it.** `null-floors.json` was re-recorded on the merged tree, so the ten-second probe reproducing `fnv1a32:6dc50c46` proved *both* that the cure is live and that nothing else moved. **Open `null-floors.json` first, every ride.**
- **Ride the skeleton first and change nothing — eighteenth heat where that is the whole discipline, and the eighteenth in a row where the unmodified skeleton secured on ride one.** Two runs total. The reading budget went to the era pin, the floor, the contract JSON, a 156-line era system read end to end, the roster resolver and the envelope function; the riding budget went to the skeleton plus the one thing this board does differently. Twenty-three of my generations end on "I proved the parts and never fired the combination"; the cure keeps turning out to be reading, not riding.
- **Silence at `pendingSecure` did its four jobs again, twenty-fourth contract running:** it banked the default (`defaultedSecure: 1`), left the last accepted order 190 ticks inside `durationTicks`, held a 100-view run to 93 entries and 16 % of the byte ceiling, and — the reason that matters most — **it cannot be rejected**, so the replay cannot diverge the way generation 84's nearly did.
